title: Sign-off, address, and the tune Lass's Candy
summary: Dave gives LaRocca's address, LaRocca explains the title Lass's Candy, and the broadcast ends.

story.theme_name: Thanks and goodbyes: closing the interview
story.community_name: Closing the interview: thanks, goodbyes and tape running out

blocks.x: Orleans yeah now Nick we we're getting very close to being completely out of time now Nick we we're getting very close to being completely out of time and I wanted to deliver this message to our listening radio audience and that is that the father of Dixieland music is still with us in good health we're happy to say in the city of New Orleans but unfortunately he's house ridden because uh he cannot get around the way he should and Nick may I have your permission to give your address over this broadcast well you can do that Dave because uh I think that there are thousands of people throughout the United States would like to know and drop a card or a letter to a famous man a man who has done a great service to music and particularly to jazz music if you would write to Nick Nick LaRocca L-A-R-O-C-C-A at 22 18 Constance Street that's C-O-N-S-T-A-N-C-E 22 18 Constance Street you will make a fine gentleman happy by knowing that his message has been finally delivered after many a year now Nick we've got time for just a little more music and the one I selected was a tune that you wrote in London called Lass's Candy will you just tell us a little bit of that before we sign off well

Lass's Candy I had already I originally named it Belgian doll and the publisher didn't like the name and uh well I changed it to Lass's Candy think of the Lass's Candy we used to have in New Orleans and and molasses that they used to manufacture and put up in cans we used to eat and I said well I didn't have no other title I give it call it Lass's Candy so in other words even at the time you were in
London England your heart and your mind had never left New Orleans I never did no well I'm here
there's nothing strange that I'm here right still living in New Orleans that's typical of New Orleans

so Nick we're going to leave our radio audience now but we will never leave your music and may I tell you on behalf of not only our radio station but of all the thousands of people who listen to jazz jamboree good health good luck and may you live to see many a happy new year as long as there's good jazz and we'll leave now with your composition called Lass's Candy stuff The End
